summary:
Review result: blocked. Nothing was built, and nothing exists that could be published. I did not finish the missing apply.py, the tests or a build.

What I checked against the staged originals (read-only, via /mnt/retro-share):
- The builder's input hashes are correct. SHOGOP3.REZ is 1,761,076 B with md5 bd1acfd9cab23d8d0b022a7633340d5a and share mtime 1999-03-09. The 525,824 bytes at offset 0x2bca8 start with 'MZ' and have md5 eb0286632a78bd488bd0f41f37114c4d. The archive header reads 'RezMgr Version 1 ... LithTech Resource File'.
- The launcher 'Play Shogo - direct engine.bat' loads the archives with -rez in the order shogo, sound, ShogoP, ShogoP2, ShogoP3, ShogoP4. LithTech takes the last one, so the v3 CShell.dll inside SHOGOP3.REZ is the one the game uses.
- The listing in the diagnosis phase's static-review-disasm.txt matches the builder's description of the original block at 0x10003546..0x1000356b: it adds each new mode to the list and never checks for a full table. The builder's cave.S redoes that same append for the case where the table is not yet full.

What I did not check: the relocation and branch-target checks, the before/after disassembly, the byte-diff of a patched output, and running any tests. None of these exist yet. I stopped this review partway through.

The diagnosis is unchanged: the in-game resolution list keeps only 12 modes per device, so 1920x1080 is missing from the default device on all four LCD boxes. No 1080p fix for Shogo's in-game menu is ready.
tests: None run. tests/python/test_patch_shogo.py does not exist, and neither the builder nor this review wrote it. apply.py does not exist, so there was nothing to run with --check or --build. Only two things were confirmed: the input md5s above, and that the original bytes at 0x10003546 match the earlier static-review listing.
risks: No patch was built, and nothing from this lane may be published. The only file in provisioning/patches/shogo/ is the builder's unbuilt, unreviewed cave.S.
Two static checks the builder listed are still not done: no relocation may fall inside the detour or cave range, and no branch may target the middle of the detour. Any future build must do both.
Changing SHOGOP3.REZ keeps its size the same. GAMESYNC notices such a change only through the file's modification time, so any future publish must stamp a fresh mtime and then be checked on a box.

Until a fix lands, 1080p is only selectable through the second d3d.ren device, whose name shows corrupted as '(d3d.ren) Primary X'. Applying a mode from that device has never been tested. The launcher already runs the game at 1920x1080, so gameplay resolution is unaffected; only the in-game menu is wrong.
The Shogo launchers' existing screenwidth/screenheight -setline mechanism is unchanged. This lane requires no FLEETRES or GAMERES change.
hw_verification_plan:
Nothing to verify on hardware until a patch is actually built and has passed its static review. When one exists, use the verifier's proven .123 procedure:
1. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Shogo" "Play Shogo - direct engine.bat" and wait 25 s.
2. Send UIKEY DOWN, DOWN, RETURN, RETURN, RETURN, DOWN, then RIGHT repeatedly. The menu is keyboard-navigable. The text flickers, so take up to 5 SCREENSHOTs per step and keep a frame whose max brightness is above 200.
3. PASS needs all of these:
   - '1920 x 1080' appears on the default '(d3d.ren) <card>' device.
   - No numeric garbage entries appear.
   - The list wraps after at most 12 entries.
   - The second device is named in full ('Primary Display Driver').
4. Apply 1920x1080 once and confirm the fullscreen frame.
5. Exit with taskkill /f /im "Client.exe". Confirm DISPLAYCFG get and the autoexec.cfg md5 are unchanged.
6. Repeat on .145, .195 and .240.

Must NOT change: the multiplayer menu must still reach the host's shogo-server list.
review_notes:
Verified: the md5 and size of SHOGOP3.REZ, the md5 and offset of the CShell.dll inside it, the -rez order in the direct-engine launcher, and that the original bytes at 0x10003546 match the earlier static-review listing.

Not verified: the builder's cave.S was not assembled or checked in this review. It stays an unbuilt, unreviewed draft.

Changed: nothing in the worktree. I did not create, edit or delete any file under provisioning/patches/shogo/ or tests/python/, and ran no git operations.

Nothing was written to the share, no box was contacted and no service was restarted. The copy of SHOGOP3.REZ and the extracted DLL I placed in my session scratchpad (outside git) have been deleted. No game data is under the git worktree.

Whoever picks this up must write apply.py and test_patch_shogo.py, and run all the static checks, before it can move from blocked.
